hints: Focus on what the two tests on Y tell you, one test means an acidic O-H group is still present, the other means a C=O group is present.
Remember how excess hot acidified dichromate treats each alcohol type, primary goes all the way to a carboxylic acid, secondary stops at a ketone, tertiary does not react.
Look for the only X that can give both a carboxylic acid and a ketone at the same time after oxidation, while still matching C7H14O2.
walkthrough:
**Decode what Y must contain**

Think like a detective. Y gives $H_2$ with $Na$, so it still has an $-OH$ or $-COOH$ group. Y gives orange crystals with 2,4-DNPH, so it must have an aldehyde or ketone $C=O$ group.

Test rules:
$$\text{-COOH or -OH} \rightarrow H_2 \text{ with Na}$$
$$\text{aldehyde or ketone} \rightarrow \text{orange ppt with 2,4-DNPH}$$

**Recall oxidation with excess hot dichromate**

Excess acidified $K_2Cr_2O_7$ under reflux is vigorous oxidation. It is the key to linking X to Y.

$$\text{primary } -CH_2OH \rightarrow -CHO \rightarrow -COOH$$
$$\text{secondary } >CHOH \rightarrow >C=O \text{ (ketone, stops there)}$$
$$\text{tertiary } >C-OH \rightarrow \text{no reaction}$$

**Apply to option A and conclude**

Option A is 4-(hydroxymethyl)cyclohexanol. It has one primary $-CH_2OH$ and one secondary ring $-OH$.

On oxidation:
$$-CH_2OH \rightarrow -COOH \text{ (gives } H_2 \text{ with Na)}$$
$$>CHOH \rightarrow >C=O \text{ (ketone, gives DNPH test)}$$
So Y is a keto-acid with both functional groups needed. This fits perfectly, so X could be A.

options.A: Contains a primary alcohol and a secondary alcohol. With excess reflux, the primary becomes $-COOH$ which reacts with Na to give H2, and the secondary becomes a ketone which gives orange crystals with 2,4-DNPH. Formula also fits C7H14O2.
options.B: Contains two secondary alcohols on a methylcyclohexane ring. Both oxidise to ketones to give a diketone. A diketone gives a positive DNPH test but has no -OH or -COOH left, so it will not give H2 with sodium.
options.C: Contains a primary $-CH_2OH$ and a tertiary alcohol. The primary oxidises to $-COOH$ but the tertiary alcohol resists oxidation. Y is a hydroxy-acid with no aldehyde or ketone, so it gives H2 with Na but fails the DNPH test.
options.D: Contains a tertiary alcohol and an aldehyde $-CHO$. The aldehyde oxidises to $-COOH$ but the tertiary alcohol is unchanged. Y is a hydroxy-acid with no carbonyl left, so it gives H2 with Na but gives no DNPH precipitate. Students choosing D forget that aldehydes do not survive excess hot dichromate.
